conviction_note: The 15 Oct release is the H1 FY27 post-close trading update, so the half's numbers are new. The decisive line is whether the Board moves FY27 off 'in line with expectations'. The 9-analyst consensus the company publishes (17 Sep) implies only ~6% FY27 organic growth against 12% underlying last year, which leaves room for 'ahead'. But the last three in-line updates moved -2.0/-2.9/+1.9, the HY and FY results were sold, and the co-CEOs made discretionary sales in August. So p_up 55 on abs 5.5 gives +0.55. That sits close to the findings' sum of +0.7: the two measurements agree that the lean is small and positive.

findings.finding: The company-published 9/9-analyst consensus (17 Sep 2026) has FY27 revenue at GBP285.4m (+8.6%). Strip out ~GBP7m of APR (8 months of a GBP10.7m/yr business) and that is only ~6% organic, or ~7% ex the GBP3.5m McCloud residual. FY26 underlying organic growth ex-McCloud was 12% and H1 FY26 organic was 8%, so the bar leaves room for 'ahead of expectations' if demand held.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Upgrade-type trading updates moved +8.9% (Oct 2023), +10.7% (Apr 2024), +14.9% (Oct 2024) and +12.4% (Feb 2025). The last three 'in line' updates moved -2.0% (Oct 2025), -2.9% (Apr 2025) and +1.9% (Apr 2026), and the HY Nov 2025 report moved -6.7% on 'in line'.
findings.why_not_priced: The bar is public, but the gap is an inference, and so is the read that it is beatable. Management reportedly guided organic growth to 'mid-to-high single digits' (snippet only, unconfirmed). If the market expected an upgrade, the stock would not trade at ~12.7x FY27 consensus EPS (310p / 24.4p), down from 344p in early August, with every one of 9 analysts Buy-rated and targets around 450p. The derating says the market expects deceleration, not an upgrade.
findings.independence: FY26 underlying-organic figure (12% ex McCloud) from a separate primary document, the 21 Apr 2026 trading update: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/xps-pensions-group--xps/post-close-trading-update/9529170

findings.finding: APR completed on 3 Aug 2026 with GBP10.7m of annual revenue. That adds roughly GBP1.8m, about +1.4pp, to H1 reported growth, and it was completed before the 17 Sep consensus update.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: M&A contribution has not been a separately visible driver; Polaris contributions were disclosed inside in-line updates that moved -2.0% and +1.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the deal is public and pre-dates the consensus update. Kept tiny only because the H1 headline growth optics get this 1.4pp lift.

findings.finding: On 7 Aug 2026, mid-way through the half being reported, co-CEOs Cuff and Bramhall sold 319,195 and 302,077 shares at 340.06p, ~GBP2.1m in total. This was a discretionary sale on top of the 22 Jul PSP tax sales, and it left each holding ~455k shares.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance found. The stock fell from 344p on 7 Aug to ~310p now, of which 9.1p was the 20 Aug ex-dividend.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for two months and most likely reflected in the ~7% ex-dividend drift since. It still matters as information about what the people who saw July trading chose to do: had they seen an upgrade coming, selling 40% of their holdings at 340p would be odd. Sized small because post-vesting diversification is routine and both still hold ~310% of salary.

findings.finding: UK bulk-annuity volume rose to GBP10.2bn in H1 2026 from GBP9.7bn, but deal count fell to 138 from 160 (Aon) and 82% of deals were under GBP100m. That is a mixed backdrop for XPS's risk-transfer advisory, which is weighted to small and mid schemes.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Risk Transfer has been cited as a growth driver in every recent update; there is no isolated reaction on it.
findings.why_not_priced: This is an industry proxy, not a company number. Fewer transactions means fewer advisory projects, but risk transfer is one service line inside Advisory, and run-on and surplus work offsets it, so it is net of the rest of the company and sized small. Fees are per transaction, so the count matters more than the GBP volume, and the headlines led with the volume rise.
findings.independence: Reinsurance News on the same Aon H1 data: https://www.reinsurancene.ws/aon-reports-strong-activity-in-uk-bulk-annuity-market-during-h126/

findings.finding: The H1 FY26 comparator still holds McCloud residual revenue. FY26 revenue ex-McCloud was GBP259.2m against GBP262.7m reported, so GBP3.5m of McCloud work sat in FY26, likely front-loaded. With Polaris now fully organic, the H1 FY27 headline growth is likely single-digit, breaking the 'double-digit growth' line every recent update led with.

baseline_tension: Mild agreement. The findings lean slightly positive (+0.7) in the same direction as priced_lean_pct (+2.1, mostly the short-squeeze component) and the +2.7% 20-day run-up. The insider sale and the McCloud comparator cut against it, and the name's recent habit of selling in-line updates is why p_up is held at 55.
language_note: The domestic RNS record (Investegate) carried the primary documents: the 5 Oct notice fixing 15 Oct, the 07:00 timestamps that settle the session, and the 10 Aug PDMR notice showing the co-CEOs' sale was discretionary on top of the PSP tax sales. English wire and aggregator copy (MarketBeat) carried the sale amounts but not the discretionary character.

The company's own IR consensus page (domestic, issuer-published) carried the 9/9-analyst FY27 bar that no English aggregator search returned; aggregators showed stale or contradictory GBP254-290m figures.
UK trade press (Professional Pensions, from Aon data) carried the H1 2026 BPA deal-count decline (138 vs 160), which the general English financial news did not connect to XPS.
lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' (guidance findings 11 of 17 on sign; median 9.0% when the guide changes): the FY27 guidance finding was raised from +0.8 to +1.2 and sized on the guidance scale, still capped well below 9 because it is an inference.

'You were right about the number and too small about the move' (realised move larger on 18 of 23 names, by a median factor of ~3): abs_move_pct was raised from 4.5 to 5.5. This is a fresh-numbers trading update, and this name's trading-update reactions have a median of ~8.9% over seven events, though the last three in-line ones moved about 2%.
The reaction history vetoes the direction, not the size: p_up stays at 55 rather than rising, because recent in-line updates and results were sold.
